role: Read-only normal-semantic versus anomaly-score comparison on existing STU206/201 caches; no fitting and no val19 access
population: All 44660 inserted normal points and all 118755 original background normal points of the same car/truck/person ground-truth classes from 76 STU201 control scans; classid null pools only these three classes

definitions.predicted_anomaly: score >= own selected expanded synthetic201 FPR95 threshold
definitions.semantic_correct: argmax of learned 19 normal class logits equals the original mapped STU normal semantic label
definitions.margin: largest normal class logit minus second largest; quantiles [0.1,0.5,0.9] over false positives
definitions.high_confidence: largest conditional19 softmax probability>=0.9; not an absolute normal support probability

synthetic201_anomaly_confidence.population: Anomaly points only from existing eligible60 synthetic201 scans

interpretation: Approximately half of inserted-normal false positives already have correct normal semantics; the coexistence is strongest for cars, including original background cars.
Truck semantic transfer itself is weak in both inserted objects and original backgrounds; semantic-score coupling cannot be assumed to fix this separate failure.
High conditional normal confidence also occurs on synthetic anomalies, so subtracting confidence after training is not established as a valid remedy.
These observations motivate a controlled jointly trained unknown-versus-normal class competition; they do not establish an improvement before its same-data development experiment.

static_audit.voxelization: SupportScans, AuxiliaryScans and frozen inference all use official=True, full actual returns, and the same nearest-to-voxel-mean representative rule
static_audit.context: Query selection occurs after full-backbone context computation; training does not encode only its supervised 512-point background subset
static_audit.labels: Same STU semantic mapping and packed-slot restoration; inserted normal deltas require genuine normal labels
static_audit.conditions: FeatureEvidence ignores conditions, so training density versus evaluation range-only conditions do not affect scores
static_audit.backbone: FrozenPerception remains eval and disables autocast; cached raw features and deployed features are FP32

training_coverage.role: Bounded cache-label/condition statistics only; no feature inference, training, new data or val19 access
training_coverage.range_definition: exp of cached float32 log-range; np.searchsorted([10,20,35], side=right); not a new geometric measurement
training_coverage.normal_cache_scope: Complete source206 and source201 original-normal prefixes, not all raw returns; 2064096/scan class-range reservation and 2012048/scan uniform normal-query budgets differ

existing_false_positive_evidence.scope: Earlier observations model, eligible60 synthetic201 population; descriptive supporting evidence, not current competition outputs

decision.equal_class_weighting: Not recommended as the next full17-class change: bicycle/motorcycle/other-vehicle/motorcyclist together receive4/17 of ordinary-normal mass despite very few and restricted-distance observations; this repeats the excessive amplification problem identified for controls.
decision.supported_target: Sidewalk ordinary-normal frequency is low relative to201 and existing errors are concentrated there; its existing206 near points are present and can be emphasized without new feature extraction. Car/fence are not missing or globally under-represented, so more weight is not established as their remedy.
decision.unfillable_by_weighting: 206 has zero bicyclist and parking training points; parking appears in201. No finite weight can create missing class or missing distance observations.
decision.next_step: Keep the already-authorized normal-donor multi-view change isolated first. If a later weighting comparison is warranted, prioritize sidewalk rather than globally equalizing all17 normal classes; retain anomaly-view and normal-control masses and semantic CE unchanged.
decision.weighting_candidate: If comparing the two proposed generic choices, prefer source206 square-root-frequency ordinary-normal BCE weighting over full class-equal weighting; never fit per201-class manual coefficients.

frequency_weighting_comparison.formula: ordinary-normal w_i = N/(sqrt(n_class)*sum_populated_classes sqrt(n_class)); multiply original ordinary-normal BCE coefficient by w_i; preserve total .45
frequency_weighting_comparison.source: All existing STU206 ordinary-normal cached points: original normals, auxiliary backgrounds, control backgrounds; exclude inserted normal controls and all anomalies
frequency_weighting_comparison.selected_candidate: sqrt-frequency balancing for ordinary-normal BCE only; preserve .05 inserted controls, .5 view-weighted anomalies, semantic CE and all cached point identities
frequency_weighting_comparison.rationale: Reduces dominant-building/vegetation mass and increases sidewalk/car/fence support without equal-class amplification of extremely rare training classes. It does not fill missing class/range support and does not establish a performance gain before evaluation.
frequency_weighting_comparison.timing: Only consider after the currently authorized multi-view-normal-control dataset comparison; do not confound the two interventions
